data.name: Nikul
data.gender_notes: Nikul is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Nikul is derived from the Sanskrit word 'nikhila', meaning 'entire' or 'comprehensive'. In Hindu mythology, Nikul refers to the idea of complete victory or triumph over challenges and obstacles. The name Nikul carries the meaning “Victory, Triumph” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Nikul usually hope their child will grow to embody victory, triumph and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the victory of the spirit over the material world.
data.etymology: Nikul belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Victory, Triumph.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nikul total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Nikul holds cultural significance for Hindus, as it evokes the idea of overcoming challenges and achieving success. It represents strength and determination, and is a reminder that no matter how difficult the circumstances, one can emerge victorious. Additionally, Nikul is not a commonly heard name, making it unique and special to those who bear it.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Nikul embodies the concept of 'Nikhil Mangalam', meaning 'all auspiciousness'. It suggests that the bearer of this name is blessed with all good things in life and is protected by the divine. It also symbolizes the idea of being complete in one's spiritual journey, having attained inner peace and harmony. The name Nikul reminds us of the power of the human spirit to overcome adversity and achieve triumph, both in worldly and spiritual matters.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Nikul in Sanskrit means "one who crushes the enemy within." It symbolizes the inner battle against negative emotions and desires, leading to self-mastery and spiritual growth.
